text:
Erik Karlsson is the name on every trade board. The trade headlines have piled up: Yardbarker reported he is "likely gone by deadline," NHLTradeRumor.com named Carolina the frontrunner, and the Maple Leafs have come up too. His own line, per Gino Hard: "Nothing Strange About That."

The production makes the case for whoever wants him. Three-time Norris winner, 19 points in 21 games, 10 of them on the power play, 23.5 minutes a night. His scoring rate, 2.31 points per 60, compares with a league rate of 1.1 for defensemen, and the Penguins have scored 7.0 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on, so the points could have been higher.

The worry is the other end. Pittsburgh's share of 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) is 46.8% with him and almost 10 points better without him. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season against top competition, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists. The offense is real; the defensive numbers are what a buyer would study.
